issues.quote: I understand it had stopped when they found him. A regulator stops with its master, Inspector.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the regulator or any clock stopping when the body was found.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a reliable clock-state clue, that the regulator stopped at a time tied to the murder, and use it to fix or bound the time of death. The sheet gives no such reading, so this unsupported claim could send the timeline in a wrong direction.

issues.quote: Whoever did this was not in a hurry
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the murderer's pace or how long the act took.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a hint that the killing took a long, unhurried stretch of time, which would widen the window for the crime beyond what the clock readings establish.

issues.quote: It strikes by its own face.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the hall clock struck eleven a moment after Dr Vauthier sat down again. It does not say how the hall clock relates to the bell or to the watches.
issues.misreading: A solver could read 'by its own face' as implying the hall clock keeps its own time separate from the bell and the watches, and so doubt its eleven o'clock strike as a reference point.
